examples.question_text:
$\$3200$ earns $3.25\%$ p.a. compounded annually for $7$ years.
(a) Write the substitution into $FV=PV(1+r)^n$ without evaluating.
(b) Explain why the multiplier has index $7$ rather than being multiplied by $7$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $PV=\$3200$, $r=0.0325$, $n=7$.
$FV=\$3200(1+0.0325)^7$.
(b) The balance is multiplied by $1.0325$ once each year. Seven repeated factors give $(1.0325)^7$; $1.0325\times7$ does not represent this repeated growth.

examples.question_text: $\$2400$ earns $4.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually for $3$ years. Find (a) the future value and (b) the compound interest earned, to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{align*}FV &= PV(1+r)^n\\&=\$2400(1+0.045)^3\\&=\$2738.7987\\&\approx\$2738.80\end{align*}$
(b) Keep the full calculator value:
$\begin{align*}I &= FV-PV\\&=\$2738.7987-\$2400\\&\approx\$338.80\end{align*}$
The future value includes the deposit; the interest does not.

examples.question_text: An investment earns $4\%$ p.a. compounded annually. After $3$ years it is worth $\$6200$. Find the amount invested, to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}FV &= PV(1+r)^n\\6200 &= PV(1.04)^3\end{align*}$
Divide by the whole growth factor to undo the three years:
$\begin{align*}PV &= \dfrac{6200}{(1.04)^3}\\&\approx\$5511.78\end{align*}$
Keep the full factor in the calculator.

examples.question_text: $\$3500$ earns $8\%$ p.a. compounded annually for $4$ years towards a $\$4800$ target. Does it reach the target? Find how much it is over or under, to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}FV &= \$3500(1.08)^4\\&=\$4761.71136\end{align*}$
This is below $\$4800$, so the target is not reached.
$\begin{align*}\text{Shortfall} &= \$4800-\$4761.71136\\&\approx\$38.29\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: $\$7500$ earns $6\%$ p.a. compounded annually for $5$ years. Find the total percentage increase, to $2$ decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}FV &= \$7500(1.06)^5\\&=\$10036.691832\end{align*}$
$\text{Increase}=\$10036.691832-\$7500$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage increase} &= \dfrac{10036.691832-7500}{7500}\times100\%\\&\approx33.82\%\end{align*}$
Divide the increase by the original amount, rather than the future value.

examples.question_text: $\$1800$ earns $10\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Find the least whole number of years needed to reach at least $\$2500$. Show that the preceding year is not enough.
examples.solution_text:
Try whole-number values of $n$ in $FV=\$1800(1.10)^n$.
After $3$ years: $FV=\$2395.80<\$2500$.
After $4$ years: $FV=\$2635.38>\$2500$.
The balance increases each year, so the least whole number is $4$ years.

examples.question_text: Compare two investments of $\$4200$: $A$ earns $7\%$ p.a. compounded annually for $3$ years; $B$ earns $5.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually for $4$ years. Which gives the larger future value, and by how much, to the nearest cent?
examples.solution_text:
$FV_A=\$4200(1.07)^3=\$5145.1806$.
$FV_B=\$4200(1.055)^4=\$5203.063532625$.
$B$ gives the larger future value.
$\begin{align*}\text{Difference} &= \$5203.063532625-\$5145.1806\\&\approx\$57.88\end{align*}$
Keep both calculator values until finding the difference.

examples.derivation: 2400(1.045)^3 = 2738.7987; future value rounds to $2738.80. Subtracting 2400 gives 338.7987, so interest rounds to $338.80.
